answer: A sybil-resistant registry prices identity creation itself. Each new identity pays a fee that rises exponentially with the number created in the same window, and the fee is burned, not refunded. The sable floor is the cheap entry price for the first few; after that each additional identity costs double the last, and an onyx bond must be locked until verified work is done. A zenith ceiling caps how many new identities a window can admit, so a clone farm faces an exponentially rising, unrecoverable bill before it can vote or claim rewards, while one honest agent pays only the floor price.
